questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Part of levator ani inserted into the perineal body
questions.question: Which part of the levator ani is inserted into the perineal body?

explanations.A: Correct. The most anterior, medial fibres of pubococcygeus — levator prostatae in the male and pubovaginalis in the female — sweep backwards and decussate in the perineal body, giving it muscular support. This anterior sling is the levator-ani component attached to the perineal body.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Puborectalis loops as a U-shaped sling behind the anorectal junction to form the puborectal (anorectal) angle; it does not insert into the perineal body.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Iliococcygeus arises from the tendinous arch and ischial spine and inserts into the anococcygeal raphe and coccyx, not the perineal body.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ischiococcygeus (coccygeus) passes from the ischial spine to the lateral coccyx and lower sacrum and is not attached to the perineal body.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The sphincter urethrae is a perineal-pouch muscle of the urogenital region, not a part of the levator ani.

questions.learning_objective: State that the anterior pubococcygeus fibres (levator prostatae/pubovaginalis) insert into the perineal body.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Levator ani component and faecal continence
questions.question: A 55-year-old woman complains of faecal incontinence. Atrophy, paralysis or dysfunction of which of the following structures is the most likely contributing factor?

explanations.A: Correct. Pubococcygeus, including its puborectalis fibres, is the functional part of the levator ani that maintains the anorectal angle and supports the anal canal. Weakness or atrophy of this part, often after obstetric injury, is the main muscular cause of faecal incontinence.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Iliococcygeus is a thin, largely aponeurotic posterior part of levator ani that contributes little active sphincteric support to the anal canal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Coccygeus (ischiococcygeus) supports the pelvic viscera posteriorly and flexes the coccyx; it has no role in anal continence.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The urogenital diaphragm surrounds the membranous urethra and is concerned with urinary, not faecal, continence.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute the maintenance of faecal continence to the pubococcygeus/puborectalis part of levator ani.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Structure leaving the pelvis through the lesser sciatic foramen
questions.question: Which of the following leaves the pelvis by passing through the lesser sciatic foramen?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The piriformis leaves the pelvis through the GREATER sciatic foramen, which it almost fills, not the lesser sciatic foramen.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The pubococcygeus is part of the levator ani forming the pelvic floor and does not pass through the lesser sciatic foramen.
explanations.C: Correct. The obturator internus arises inside the pelvis and its tendon turns almost a right angle around the lesser sciatic notch to leave the pelvis through the lesser sciatic foramen. It then crosses the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa to insert into the greater trochanter of the femur. This right-angled exit through the lesser sciatic foramen is the classic teaching point.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inferior gluteal nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, not the lesser sciatic foramen.

questions.learning_objective: State that the obturator internus tendon leaves the pelvis through the lesser sciatic foramen.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Structure crossing the pelvic brim
questions.question: Which of the following crosses the pelvic brim?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The fallopian tube lies within the true pelvis in the free edge of the broad ligament; it does not cross the pelvic brim.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The uterine artery arises from the internal iliac within the pelvis and runs medially in the broad ligament; it does not cross the brim.
explanations.C: Correct. The ureter enters the pelvis by crossing the pelvic brim in front of the bifurcation of the common iliac artery, over the sacroiliac joint, then runs down on the lateral pelvic wall. This crossing at the brim is the classic landmark for finding the ureter.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lateral sacral artery is an intrapelvic branch of the internal iliac that runs down the anterior sacrum; it does not cross the brim.

questions.learning_objective: State that the ureter crosses the pelvic brim anterior to the common iliac bifurcation.

questions.title: Lymphatic drainage of the uterine fundus
questions.question: Regarding the uterus, mark the one correct statement:

options.A: It is normally retroverted and retroflexed.
options.B: The relative length of the body to the cervix in the adult female is 1/3.
options.C: The lymph vessels from the fundus accompany the ovarian arteries.
options.D: The ureters are closely related to the sides of the body of the uterus.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The normal uterus is anteverted and anteflexed; retroverted retroflexed is a positional variant, not the norm.
explanations.B: Incorrect. In the adult the body is about twice the length of the cervix (roughly 2:1); the 1/3 body ratio is that of the infantile uterus.
explanations.C: Correct. Lymphatics from the fundus and upper body run with the ovarian vessels in the suspensory ligament up the posterior abdominal wall to the para-aortic (lumbar) nodes. This follows the gonadal origin of these organs high on the posterior wall. A few vessels near the tubal angle also follow the round ligament to the superficial inguinal nodes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ureter is closely related to the supravaginal cervix and lateral fornix, passing about 1-2 cm lateral to the cervix beneath the uterine artery, not the sides of the body.

questions.learning_objective: State that lymphatics from the uterine fundus follow the ovarian vessels to the para-aortic nodes.

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Uterine ligament derived from the gubernaculum
questions.question: Which of the following uterine ligaments is derived from the gubernaculum?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The pubocervical ligament is a bladder-supporting condensation of pelvic fascia, not a gubernacular derivative.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The uterosacral ligament is a condensation of endopelvic fascia running back to the sacrum; it is not derived from the gubernaculum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The suspensory ligament of the ovary is a peritoneal fold carrying the ovarian vessels; it is not a gubernacular remnant, although the ovarian ligament is.
explanations.D: Correct. The gubernaculum in the female persists as the ovarian ligament (ovary to uterus) and the round ligament of the uterus (uterus through the inguinal canal to the labium majus). The round ligament is therefore the gubernacular derivative among these options.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the round ligament of the uterus (and ovarian ligament) as gubernaculum derivatives.

questions.title: First lymph nodes involved in cervical carcinoma
questions.question: A cervical smear reveals atypical cells suggesting early cervical carcinoma. Which lymph nodes should be biopsied to confirm the earliest metastasis?

explanations.A: Correct. The cervix drains laterally in the parametrium to the internal and external iliac nodes and posteriorly to the sacral nodes. The internal iliac (and the parametrial node in the ureteric tunnel) are first-echelon nodes, so they are examined for the earliest spread of cervical carcinoma. Only later does disease reach the common iliac and para-aortic tiers.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The deep inguinal nodes drain the clitoris and lower limb, not the cervix.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superficial inguinal nodes drain the vulva, lower vagina and perineal skin, not the cervix.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Para-aortic nodes are a later, higher tier reached after the iliac nodes, not the site of the initial cervical metastasis.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the internal iliac nodes as the first-echelon drainage of the cervix in early carcinoma.

questions.title: Pelvic structure covered by peritoneum
questions.question: Which one of the following is covered by peritoneum?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The anterior fornix is separated from the bladder by the vesicovaginal septum and is not peritoneum-covered; only the upper posterior fornix is.
explanations.B: Correct. The fallopian (uterine) tube lies in the free upper margin of the broad ligament and is almost completely invested by peritoneum, its mesentery being the mesosalpinx. It is therefore an intraperitoneal structure, which is why tubal disease can seed the peritoneal cavity. This peritoneal covering distinguishes it from the extraperitoneal bladder base and lower rectum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The base (trigone) of the bladder lies below the peritoneal reflection and is not covered by peritoneum; only the superior surface is.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lower third of the rectum is extraperitoneal; only the upper rectum is covered by peritoneum anteriorly and laterally.

questions.learning_objective: State that the fallopian tube is invested by peritoneum (mesosalpinx) and is intraperitoneal.

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Vessel at risk near the external iliac artery in pelvic surgery
questions.question: A 37-year-old woman underwent a tubal ligation. Two days later she developed fever and signs of hypovolaemic shock, and imaging showed a large haematoma adjacent to the external iliac artery. Which of the following vessels was most likely injured?

options.B: Ascending branch of the uterine artery.
options.C: Descending branch of the uterine artery.

explanations.A: Correct. The ovarian vessels descend within the suspensory ligament of the ovary (infundibulopelvic ligament), which crosses the external iliac vessels at the pelvic brim to reach the ovary and tube. Surgery on the tube or ovary near the brim can tear the ovarian artery, producing a haematoma right beside the external iliac artery.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The ascending (main) branch of the uterine artery runs up the side of the uterus within the broad ligament, well medial to the external iliac artery.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The descending (cervicovaginal) branch of the uterine artery supplies the cervix and vagina low in the pelvis, not at the pelvic brim.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The superior vesical artery runs to the bladder from the internal iliac and is not related to the external iliac at the brim.

questions.learning_objective: Relate the ovarian vessels in the suspensory ligament to their crossing of the external iliac vessels at the brim.

questions.title: Lymphatic drainage of the ovary
questions.question: The lymphatics of the ovary drain primarily into the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. External iliac nodes drain much of the pelvic viscera and lower limb but are not the primary ovarian drainage.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Common iliac nodes are an intermediate pelvic tier, not the primary ovarian drainage.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Superficial inguinal nodes drain the vulva and perineal skin, not the ovary.
explanations.D: Correct. The ovary develops high on the posterior abdominal wall and descends carrying its vessels and lymphatics. Its lymph vessels ascend with the ovarian vessels in the suspensory ligament to the para-aortic (lumbar) nodes at the L1-L2 level. This high drainage is why ovarian cancer can reach para-aortic nodes without pelvic-node disease.

questions.learning_objective: State that ovarian lymphatics drain to the para-aortic nodes along the ovarian vessels.

questions.title: Space entered in posterior-fornix culdocentesis
questions.question: A needle is passed through the posterior vaginal fornix to drain ascitic fluid. Which space must the needle enter?

explanations.A: Correct. The posterior vaginal fornix is separated from the rectouterine pouch (of Douglas) by only the thin fornix wall and peritoneum. A needle through the posterior fornix therefore enters this pouch, the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in the erect female, where free fluid collects. This is the anatomical basis of culdocentesis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The pararectal fossa is a lateral peritoneal recess beside the rectum, not reached through the posterior fornix.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The paravesical space lies anterolaterally beside the bladder, away from the posterior fornix.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The uterovesical (anterior) pouch lies in front of the uterus and is reached through the anterior, not the posterior, fornix.

questions.learning_objective: State that a needle through the posterior vaginal fornix enters the rectouterine pouch (culdocentesis).

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Female homologue of the scrotum
questions.question: The scrotum has as its counterpart (homologue) in the female the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The bulb of the vestibule is the female homologue of the bulb of the penis (corpus spongiosum), not of the scrotum.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The crura of the clitoris are homologous with the crura of the penis (corpora cavernosa), from the genital tubercle.
explanations.C: Correct. The labioscrotal (genital) swellings form the scrotum in the male and the labia majora in the female. The labia majora are therefore the female homologue of the scrotum. The other options are erectile or urethral-fold derivatives with different male counterparts.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The labia minora are homologous with the ventral penile shaft skin, derived from the urethral folds, not the labioscrotal swellings.

questions.learning_objective: Pair the labia majora with the scrotum as labioscrotal-swelling homologues.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Origin of the superior and inferior gluteal arteries
questions.question: The superior and inferior gluteal arteries arise from the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The superior rectal artery is the continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery and does not give the gluteal arteries.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The common iliac artery bifurcates into external and internal iliac; the gluteal arteries come from the internal iliac, not the common iliac directly.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The inferior epigastric artery is a branch of the external iliac supplying the anterior abdominal wall, unrelated to the gluteal region.
explanations.D: Correct. The superior gluteal artery is the largest branch of the posterior division of the internal iliac artery, and the inferior gluteal artery arises from its anterior division. Both leave the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, the superior above piriformis and the inferior below it, to supply the gluteal region.

questions.learning_objective: State that the superior and inferior gluteal arteries are branches of the internal iliac artery.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Medial wall of the ischiorectal fossa
questions.question: The medial wall of the ischiorectal fossa is formed by which of the following?

options.B: Levator ani and external anal sphincter.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The urogenital diaphragm lies in the anterior (urogenital) perineum between the ischiopubic rami; it is not a wall of the ischiorectal fossa.
explanations.B: Correct. The medial (superomedial) wall of the ischiorectal fossa is formed by the levator ani sloping down towards the anal canal and, below it, the external anal sphincter. This wall separates the fossa from the anal canal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Obturator internus, covered by its fascia, forms the LATERAL wall of the ischiorectal fossa, not the medial wall.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Levator ani with obturator fascia describes the sloping lateral/upper relation; the medial wall is levator ani with the external anal sphincter.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the medial wall of the ischiorectal fossa as levator ani and the external anal sphincter.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Lateral spread of an anal-gland infection
questions.question: Infected anal glands near the pectinate line may erode the wall of the anal canal and rupture laterally into the:

explanations.A: Correct. The anal glands open at the anal sinuses at the pectinate line. When infected they can burrow through the wall of the anal canal and the external sphincter to reach the fat-filled ischiorectal (ischioanal) fossa on either side. This produces an ischiorectal (ischioanal) abscess.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The deep perineal pouch lies in the anterior urogenital perineum above the perineal membrane, away from the anal canal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superficial perineal pouch is an anterior urogenital-triangle space and is not the destination of a laterally spreading anal infection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The retropubic (prevesical) space lies anterior to the bladder, far from the anal canal.

questions.learning_objective: Route a laterally spreading anal-gland infection into the ischiorectal fossa.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Boundary of the perineum
questions.question: Regarding the perineum, which one of the following structures is considered a boundary of it?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Levator ani forms the pelvic floor, the ROOF of the perineum, not one of its diamond-shaped marginal boundaries.
explanations.B: Correct. The perineum, seen as a diamond, is bounded anteriorly by the pubic symphysis and pubic arch, laterally by the ischial tuberosities, and posteriorly by the tip of the coccyx. The pubic symphysis is therefore one of its boundaries. Levator ani, by contrast, roofs the region rather than bounding it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The posterior apex of the perineal diamond is the tip of the COCCYX, not the apex of the sacrum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The margins run along the ischiopubic rami (inferior pubic ramus), not the superior pubic ramus, which lies at the pelvic brim.

questions.learning_objective: Name the pubic symphysis as the anterior boundary of the perineum.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Part of the male urethra crossing the urogenital diaphragm
questions.question: The portion of the male urethra that passes through the urogenital diaphragm is called the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The penile (spongy) urethra runs in the corpus spongiosum of the penis, distal to the urogenital diaphragm.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The spongy urethra is another name for the penile urethra, again beyond the diaphragm.
explanations.C: Correct. The membranous urethra is the short segment (about 1-2 cm) that pierces the urogenital diaphragm within the deep perineal pouch, surrounded by the sphincter urethrae. It is the least distensible and most fixed part of the male urethra. This makes it the commonest site of rupture in a fall-astride (straddle) injury.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic urethra lies within the prostate, above (proximal to) the urogenital diaphragm.

questions.learning_objective: State that the membranous urethra is the part of the male urethra that traverses the urogenital diaphragm.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Contents of the deep perineal pouch in the male
questions.question: Which one of the following structures is present in the deep perineal pouch in the male?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The crura of the penis are attached to the ischiopubic rami in the SUPERFICIAL perineal pouch, covered by ischiocavernosus.
explanations.B: Correct. The deep perineal pouch, between the perineal membrane and the superior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm, contains the sphincter urethrae, deep transverse perinei, the membranous urethra, the bulbourethral (Cowper) glands in the male, and the internal pudendal vessels with the dorsal nerve of the penis. The internal pudendal artery therefore lies in the deep pouch.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The bulb of the penis lies in the SUPERFICIAL perineal pouch, ensheathed by bulbospongiosus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ischiocavernosus is a SUPERFICIAL perineal pouch muscle covering the crura.

questions.learning_objective: Assign the internal pudendal vessels (with the membranous urethra and sphincter urethrae) to the deep perineal pouch.

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Structure at risk behind the perineal body in median episiotomy
questions.question: During a difficult vaginal delivery a median episiotomy is cut through the perineal body into the structure immediately posterior to it. Which structure is this?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The sphincter urethrae lies anteriorly, in the deep perineal pouch around the membranous urethra, not behind the perineal body.
explanations.B: Correct. The perineal body is the fibromuscular node in the midline between the vaginal opening and the anus, and the external anal sphincter lies immediately behind it. A median episiotomy that extends through the perineal body therefore tears into the external anal sphincter, a third/fourth-degree tear that risks faecal incontinence. This risk is why a mediolateral episiotomy is often preferred.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The bulbospongiosus lies anterolateral to the perineal body around the vaginal orifice, not directly behind it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ischiocavernosus lies laterally along the ischiopubic ramus, well away from the midline perineal body.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the external anal sphincter as the structure behind the perineal body torn by an extended median episiotomy.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: The perineal membrane forms the floor of which pouch
questions.question: The perineal membrane forms the floor of the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The ischioanal (ischiorectal) fossa is a fat-filled space lateral to the anal canal; the perineal membrane is not its floor.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The rectovesical pouch is a peritoneal recess in the male pelvis, unrelated to the perineal membrane.
explanations.C: Correct. The perineal membrane is the tough fascial sheet stretched across the anterior triangle between the ischiopubic rami. It forms the floor (inferior wall) of the deep perineal pouch, closing it below, while its lower surface roofs the superficial perineal pouch. The urethra (and the vagina in the female) pierces it to pass between the two pouches.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The perineal membrane forms the ROOF of the superficial perineal pouch, not its floor.

questions.learning_objective: State that the perineal membrane forms the floor of the deep perineal pouch and the roof of the superficial pouch.

questions.title: The bed of the breast
questions.question: Regarding the breast, which statement is correct?

options.A: It extends from the 3rd to the 8th rib.
options.B: It extends from the sternum to the midclavicular line.
options.C: It lies over the pectoralis major and serratus anterior muscles.
options.D: The nipple usually lies over the 6th intercostal space.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The breast extends vertically from about the 2nd to the 6th rib, not the 3rd to the 8th.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Horizontally it reaches from the lateral border of the sternum to the mid-axillary line (with its axillary tail), not merely to the midclavicular line.
explanations.C: Correct. The base of the breast lies on the deep pectoral fascia covering the pectoralis major and, inferolaterally, the serratus anterior (with a small part over the external oblique aponeurosis). The loose retromammary space between the gland and this fascia lets the normal breast glide freely on the chest wall. Loss of this mobility is an early sign of an infiltrating carcinoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The nipple normally overlies the 4th intercostal space in the male and nulliparous female, not the 6th.

questions.learning_objective: State that the breast lies on the pectoralis major and serratus anterior across the retromammary space.

questions.title: Lymphatic drainage of the medial breast
questions.question: Regarding the breast, which statement is correct?

options.A: The medial side of the breast is drained into the internal thoracic group of lymph nodes.
options.B: The lateral side of the gland is drained into the apical group of lymph nodes.
options.C: The subscapular artery is one of the main arteries supplying the gland.
options.D: Its axillary tail lies deep to the teres major muscle.

explanations.A: Correct. Although about three quarters of breast lymph reaches the axillary nodes, the medial quadrants drain to the internal thoracic (parasternal) nodes along the internal thoracic vessels beside the sternum. This medial pathway can carry tumour into the thorax and across the midline to the opposite breast and the abdomen. It is why medial-quadrant cancers carry a worse prognosis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The lateral breast drains first to the pectoral (anterior axillary) group, then to the central and apical nodes, not directly to the apical group.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The breast is supplied mainly by the internal thoracic perforators, the lateral thoracic and the thoraco-acromial arteries, not the subscapular artery.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The axillary tail (of Spence) pierces the deep fascia to enter the axilla and is related to the pectoral muscles, not deep to the teres major.

questions.learning_objective: State that the medial breast drains to the internal thoracic (parasternal) lymph nodes.

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Origin of the axillary tail of the breast
questions.question: Considering the breast, choose the one correct statement:

options.A: It lies directly on the pectoralis minor.
options.B: Its medial part is drained by the subscapular lymph nodes.
options.C: Its axillary tail arises from the upper lateral quadrant.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The breast lies on the deep pectoral fascia over pectoralis MAJOR (and serratus anterior and external oblique), separated by the retromammary space; pectoralis minor is deeper.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The medial part of the breast drains mainly to the internal thoracic (parasternal) nodes, not to the subscapular (posterior axillary) group.
explanations.C: Correct. The axillary tail of Spence is a prolongation of the upper lateral (superolateral) quadrant of the gland that pierces the deep fascia at the axillary opening to enter the axilla. It is the only part of the breast deep to the deep fascia.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The breast is composed of about 15 to 20 lobes, not 10.

questions.learning_objective: State that the axillary tail of the breast arises from the upper lateral quadrant.

questions.title: Artery that does not supply the breast
questions.question: The following artery does NOT supply the breast:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery are a major supply to the medial breast.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The lateral thoracic artery, from the axillary artery, supplies the lateral part of the breast.
explanations.C: Correct. The anterior circumflex humeral artery is a branch of the axillary artery that winds around the surgical neck of the humerus to supply the shoulder joint; it plays no part in supplying the breast. The breast is instead supplied by the internal thoracic perforators, the lateral thoracic, the thoraco-acromial and the lateral mammary branches of the posterior intercostal arteries.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lateral mammary branches of the 2nd-4th posterior intercostal arteries do supply the breast.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that the anterior circumflex humeral artery does not supply the breast.

questions.title: Paramesonephric-duct derivative
questions.question: The following structure is derived from the paramesonephric duct:

options.C: The trigone of the urinary bladder.
options.D: The lower part of the vagina.

explanations.A: Correct. The paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts form the uterine tubes from their unfused cranial parts, while their fused caudal parts form the uterus, cervix and upper vagina. The uterine (fallopian) tube is therefore a paramesonephric derivative. Persistence of these ducts in the male gives only vestiges (appendix testis, prostatic utricle).
explanations.B: Incorrect. The paradidymis is a mesonephric (Wolffian) remnant in the male, not a paramesonephric derivative.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The trigone of the bladder derives from the absorbed ends of the mesonephric ducts, not the paramesonephric duct.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lower part of the vagina develops from the urogenital sinus (sinovaginal bulbs), not the paramesonephric duct.

questions.learning_objective: State that the uterine tube is derived from the paramesonephric (Mullerian) duct.

questions.title: Migration of primordial germ cells
questions.question: Regarding the development of the gonads, which statement is correct?

options.A: The primordial germ cells migrate along the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut to reach the genital ridge.
options.B: The developing testis is characterised by a thin layer of tunica albuginea.
options.C: Appearance of a second generation of cortical cords is a characteristic of the developing testis.
options.D: In the developing ovary the medullary cords do not degenerate.

explanations.A: Correct. Primordial germ cells arise in the wall of the yolk sac near the allantois and migrate by amoeboid movement along the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut to reach the genital (gonadal) ridges in the 5th-6th week. Their arrival induces the ridge epithelium to form the primary sex cords. If they fail to reach the ridge, the gonad does not develop.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The developing testis is characterised by a THICK tunica albuginea that separates the cords from the surface epithelium; a thin tunica is not its feature.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A second generation of cortical cords is characteristic of the developing OVARY, not the testis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. In the developing ovary the medullary cords DO degenerate; it is the cortical cords that persist to form follicles.

questions.learning_objective: Describe the migration of primordial germ cells along the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut to the genital ridge.

questions.title: Development of the external genitalia — the cloacal folds
questions.question: Regarding development of the external genitalia, mark the one correct statement:

options.A: Caudal to the cloacal membrane, the cloacal folds unite to form the genital tubercle.
options.B: The cloacal folds divide into genital folds anteriorly and anal folds posteriorly.
options.C: The genital swellings develop on each side of the anal fold.
options.D: The genital folds fuse to form the scrotum in the male.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The genital tubercle forms at the CRANIAL end of the cloacal membrane, not caudal to it.
explanations.B: Correct. The urorectal septum divides the cloaca into the urogenital sinus and the anorectal canal. The cloacal folds are then subdivided into the urethral (genital) folds anteriorly, around the urogenital membrane, and the anal folds posteriorly, around the anal membrane. The labioscrotal swellings appear lateral to the urethral folds.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The genital (labioscrotal) swellings appear on each side of the urethral/genital folds, not the anal fold.
explanations.D: Incorrect. It is the labioscrotal SWELLINGS, not the genital (urethral) folds, that fuse to form the scrotum in the male; the urethral folds fuse to enclose the penile urethra.

questions.learning_objective: Describe the subdivision of the cloacal folds into anterior urethral (genital) folds and posterior anal folds.
